correctness.rationale: The graph has diameter two. An omitted disjoint pair cannot be strongly resolved by a third vertex. For an omitted intersecting pair u,v, take a line w through a point of v outside u and not lying in their span. The line w is disjoint from u, so w must be selected, and u–v–w is a geodesic. Strong resolution therefore reduces exactly to the clique condition for the omitted set. Every clique of size at least two is either concurrent at a unique point or nonconcurrent in a unique plane: a third line missing the intersection of the first two must lie in their span, and then prohibits any outside line. Counting the two classes gives the stated polynomial. The size counts at d=4 are family-specific, as the final sentence of the Finding indicates: the total at the common size is P+T, not P or T separately. For a bounded independent check, forming the 35 binary lines as triples {u,v,u XOR v} and recursively appending only higher-index adjacent lines gave coefficients 1,35,315,945,1050,630,210,30, with 30 maximal cliques all of size 7. This check is not used as a proof for general q,d. The frozen verification source was inspected, not run.

evidence: Two distinct pencils share at most one line, and two distinct plane tops share at most one by the dimension of the intersection of their planes. A mixed pair shares q+1 lines precisely when its point is in its plane, and otherwise none. There are sT such incident flags.

For k≥2 there can be at most one containing clique of each type. Inclusion–exclusion immediately gives P binom(r,k) + T binom(s,k) − sT binom(q+1,k); sizes 0 and 1 are trivial. Minimal sets and their sizes are exactly the complements of the published maximal configurations.
